resolved_in_v1_8_1.G1: MARGIN_RESERVE_USDT=2000.0 derived as one initial-margin tranche: R=(C-R)/(L+1) => R=C/(L+2)=2000. POSITION_CAPITAL_USDT=8000. Sizing q=(C-R)L/((L+1)S_in). Reserve constant across leverage sensitivities. T16 exact invariant is now relative to POSITION_CAPITAL_USDT.
resolved_in_v1_8_1.G2: FUNDING_COUNTS_TOWARD_MARGIN=True. Both signs move the futures wallet.
resolved_in_v1_8_1.G3: POST_LIQUIDATION_RULE='unwind'. No rehedging. Perp terminates at the simulated liquidation fill; spot unwinds at the first causally executable spot open after the liquidation bar, using M6b roll-forward; naked-spot exposure recorded as tracking error.
resolved_in_v1_8_1.G4: EVENT_ORDER='funding_then_margin_then_topup_then_liquidation'. Corrects the v1.8 docstring/notes which said liquidation->topup->funding and did not match intent.
resolved_in_v1_8_1.G5: Liquidation accounting fixed: scheduled perp exit price unused after forced close; no ordinary cost_perp_out; price loss appears exactly once in q(P_in-P_liq); liquidation_fee_usdt carries only the clearance fee; explicit liquidation_ts/fill and spot_unwind_ts/fill fields added.

H14.item: BTCUSDT USD-M liquidation clearance fee rate and forced-fill execution semantics
H14.status: UNRESOLVED - authoritative rate not obtainable from this environment

established.fact: A Liquidation Clearance Fee exists and is computed from an applicable rate times the notional value of the position
Liquidation trigger is Collateral = Initial Collateral + Realized PnL + Unrealized PnL < Maintenance Margin (matches this protocol's condition)

Smart Liquidation offloads via an Immediate-or-Cancel order; the unfilled remainder becomes a Bankrupt Position handled by the Futures Insurance Fund. The fill is therefore a market IOC and can be worse than the trigger price for a short.

H15.resolution: ADOPTED AS A PARTIAL PROXY, explicitly not an exact A2 reconstruction (RATE_SOURCE_FIDELITY='partial_proxy_not_exact_A2').
H15.v4_excluded: Phase 8 does NOT transition to Aave V4. V4 changes the borrowing-rate architecture through collateral-dependent risk premiums, while V3 continues to exist as an available market. V4 Ethereum launch 2026-03-30 is recorded for reference only.
H15.consequence: The layer-3/V4 asymmetry raised in v1.8.2 section 26.3 is RESOLVED: layer 2 and layer 3 are both on V3 Core.
H15.rate_series: variable borrow APR - an explicit proxy specialisation with no basis in A2 (V1/V2 also offered stable rates); reported as such
H15.basket: USDT/USDC/DAI equal-weight mean; all three components REQUIRED; silent composition change is refused
H15.sampling: daily point-in-time snapshot at 00:00 UTC using only chain state at or before that timestamp; no interpolation or smoothing
H15.provenance: splice dates, snapshot hour, per-component raw values and the missing-day list must be recorded in the artifact
H15.sensitivity_retained: Kenneth-French daily RF remains the preregistered sensitivity, not a replacement

H16.defect: point_in_time_rate() defaulted to MAX_STALE_SECONDS = 9h, which is the funding-series constant. A2's Aave rate input is daily, so 9h would stale it mid-morning of the same calendar day.
H16.resolution: MAX_STALE_SECONDS retired. FUNDING_MAX_STALE_SECONDS = 9*3600 and RATE_MAX_STALE_SECONDS = 24*3600 introduced; point_in_time_rate() uses the rate-specific constant.
H16.snapshot_age_semantics: A daily Aave observation represents protocol state sampled at 00:00 UTC; its age is measured from that daily snapshot, not from the last underlying reserve-update event.
tests: T42 valid through the same UTC day
T43 stale past the frozen horizon when the next snapshot is missing
T44 the 9h funding constant cannot affect rho
T46 no interpolation across missing days

source_sensitivity.rule: if sign(disposition under the Aave proxy) != sign(disposition under the Kenneth-French RF sensitivity) then classify as source_sensitive, NOT GO
source_sensitivity.note: A third outcome distinct from both GO and NO-GO: the conclusion would be about the rate-source choice rather than about the mechanism.
